s: And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat «Aram»;

G630.d: to set free, release; to let go, dismiss; to depart
s: And he «sent» «away» the multitude, and took ship, and came into the coasts of Magdala.
And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her «away».

G622.d: to destroy utterly, destroy, kill; to lose utterly; to perish; of things; of persons; to be lost
s: And his disciples came to him, and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we «perish».
Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might «destroy» him.
But go rather to the «lost» sheep of the house of Israel.

G649.d: to send away, to dispatch; to send; of persons; of things; to send away, dismiss
s: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that «sent» me.
And he shall «send» Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you:

G611.d: to separate, distinguish; to choose; to answer; in general sense; to begin to speak, take up the conversation
s: He «answered» and said unto them, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man;

G647.d: τό (ἀφίστημι), 1. in cl., only in phrase ἀποστασίου δίκη, an action against a freedman for forsaking his προστάτης (Dem.). 2. In LXX, βιβλίον ἀποστασίου, a bill of divorce: in same sense ἀ. alone (MM, see word), (for other late exx., see MM, l.with; Kennedy, Sources, 121).† (AS)
s: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of «divorcement», and to put her away.

G620.d: to leave, leave behind; to be reserved, remain; to desert, abandon
s: Erastus abode at Corinth: but Trophimus have I «left» at Miletum sick.
There «remaineth» therefore a rest to the people of God.

G654.d: to turn away, remove; to turn away from allegiance, pervert; to turn back, return; to turn oneself away from
s: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee «turn» not thou «away».
But we are not of them who draw back unto «perdition»; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.
Whose end is «destruction», whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.)
But when his disciples saw it, they had indignation, saying, To what purpose is this «waste»?
And seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came, if «haply» he might find any thing thereon: and when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves; for the time of figs was not yet.
And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: «depart» from me, ye that work iniquity.
And he «touched» her hand, and the fever left her: and she arose, and ministered unto them.
And the «apostles» said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.
Provide neither gold, nor «silver», nor brass in your purses,

G601.d: of things; of persons; In LXX and NT, in special sense of divine revelation
s: Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is «revealed».
And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and «kill» him.
And they shall scourge him, and «put» him to «death»: and the third day he shall rise again.
Saying, The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be «slain», and be raised the third day.
But I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be «restored» to you the sooner.
And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing «idle» in the marketplace,

G659.d: to put off or aside; to put of from oneself as a garment; to put of, lay aside; to stow away, put
s: But now ye also «put» «off» all these; anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, filthy communication out of your mouth.
And he sent, and «beheaded» John in the prison.
But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s «money».
And he cast down the «pieces» of «silver» in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.
I have coveted no man’s «silver», or gold, or apparel.

G645.d: to draw off or away, tear away
s: And, behold, one of them which were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and «drew» his sword, and struck a servant of the high priest’s, and smote off his ear.

When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and «washed» his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.
And when they looked, they saw that the stone was «rolled» «away»: for it was very great.
For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any «thing» kept «secret», but that it should come abroad.

G639.d: to be at a loss, be perplexed; be in doubt
s: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are «perplexed», but not in despair;

G657.d: to take leave of; to forsake
s: And when he had «sent» them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.

G618.d: to receive from another; to receive as one's due; to receive back; to take apart or aside
s: To redeem them that were under the law, that we might «receive» the adoption of sons.

G609.d: to cut off; to mutilate oneself, have oneself mutilated
s: I would they were even «cut» «off» which trouble you.
And if thy hand «offend» thee, «cut» it «off»: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:

G650.d: to defraud, deprive of, despoil; endure deprivation; bereft of
s: Nay, ye do wrong, and «defraud», and that your brethren.

G635.d: to cause to go astray; to be led astray
s: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some «coveted» after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

G667.d: to carry off, bear, or lead away
s: And he «carried» me «away» in the spirit to a great and high mountain, and shewed me that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God,

G602.d: a reveal­ing, revelation; a manifestion from God
s: How that by «revelation» he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words,
And went again into the judgment hall, and saith unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no «answer».
Then went the devils out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were «choked».
And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, «shake» «off» the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do «wipe» «off» against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.
Even the mystery which hath been «hid» from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints:
And as he said these things unto them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, and to provoke him to «speak» of many things:

G626.d: to defend; to defend one's self
s: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall «answer»:

When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath «shut» to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:

G658.d: to bring to an end, complete, accomplish
s: Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is «finished», bringeth forth death.
And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and «licked» his sores.

G687.d: interrog. particle, implying anxiety or impatience, "quite rare and only in Luke and Paul, therefore a literary word" (Bl., §77, 2). 1. (num igitur) expecting a neg. reply, ἆρά γε,. 2. (ergone) in apodosis, expecting an affirm. reply, (Bl., l.with; Lft., Ga., in l.; MM, see word). † (AS)

G606.d: to be laid up, in store, laid away; to be reserved
s: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept «laid» «up» in a napkin:
And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with «perplexity»; the sea and the waves roaring;

G629.d: release effected by pay­ment of ransom, redemption, deliverance
s: Being justified freely by his grace through the «redemption» that is in Christ Jesus:
These words spake his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put «out» of the «synagogue».

G651.d: In NT, the office of an Apostle of Christ, apostleship
s: By whom we have received grace and «apostleship», for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:
And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them «utterance».
Cretes and «Arabians», we do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God.

G683.d: to thrust away from oneself, refuse, reject
s: But he that did his neighbour wrong thrust him «away», saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us?
And immediately there «fell» from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.
So they, being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, departed unto Seleucia; and from thence they «sailed» to Cyprus.

G673.d: to separate, part asunder; to separate oneself
s: And the heaven «departed» as a scroll when it is rolled together; and every mountain and island were moved out of their places.
Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and «Apollonia», they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:

G697.d: Hill of Pres or Mars, Areopagus; also, the Court of Areopagus, the highest tribunal of Athens
s: Then Paul stood in the midst of «Mars»’ hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.

G698.d: a judge of the Court of Areopagus
s: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the «Areopagite», and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
For while one saith, I am of Paul; and another, I am of «Apollos»; are ye not carnal?
For a certain man named Demetrius, a «silversmith», which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made «silver» shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;

G643.d: to pack and carry off; to pack and remove one's goods; to equip, make ready; to make one's preparations
s: And after those days we «took» up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
Mine «answer» to them that do examine me is this,
Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my «defence» which I make now unto you.

G628.d: to wash off, wash away; to wash off oneself
s: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and «wash» «away» thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

G677.d: not causing to stumble; not stumbling, without offence, blameless
s: Give none «offence», neither to the Jews, nor to the Gentiles, nor to the church of God:
But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should «cast» «themselves» first into the sea, and get to land:
And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as «Appii» forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
Whose mouth is full of «cursing» and bitterness:

G603.d: -ας, ἡ (ἀποκαραδοκέω, used by Aq. in for חוּל; ἀπό, κάρα the head, δοκέω, in Ion., to watch), to watch with outstretched head, watch anxiously (Polyb., π.; see Deiss., LAE, 374.5, 377 f.), (Lft., in l; Cremer, 177).† (AS)
s: For the «earnest» «expectation» of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.

G662.d: to be quite bold, make a bold venture
s: But Esaias is «very» «bold», and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me.

G663.d: to cut of; steepness, sharpness; severity
s: Behold therefore the goodness and «severity» of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.
Let love be without dissimulation. «Abhor» that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.
But we had the «sentence» of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead:
Therefore I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use «sharpness», according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.
For this Agar is mount Sinai in «Arabia», and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children.
And that he might «reconcile» both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby:
Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my «absence», work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all «pleasing», being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;
Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to «enjoy» the pleasures of sin for a season;

G665.d: to turn away; to turn oneself away from
s: Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such «turn» «away».
And to our beloved «Apphia», and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:
I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will «repay» it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.

G616.d: safe delivery," to bring forth, give birth to
s: Then when lust hath conceived, it «bringeth» «forth» sin: and sin, when it is finished, «bringeth» «forth» death.
Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither «shadow» of turning.
And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of «persons» judgeth according to every man’s work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear:
For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean «escaped» from them who live in error.

G623.d: τος, ὁ (present ptcp. of ἀπολλύω), Apollyon, i.e. the Destroyer: (cf. Ἀβάδδων). (Cremer, 453; DB, i, 125, 172.) † (AS)
s: And they had a king over them, which is the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in the Hebrew tongue is Abaddon, but in the Greek tongue hath his name «Apollyon».
